notes:
I couldn't do the research this turn, so I have no notes on Psalm 84 for you. My first try was to open seven commentary pages at once: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, Precept Austin, Augustine on New Advent, and the NET Bible notes. That went over the tool's usage limit. My second try, opening only the Enduring Word page, was blocked because I had no tool calls left for this turn. None of the pages loaded.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for each point. Since I read nothing, I can't write any verse notes. Doing so would mean filling them in from memory, which would break both rules.

If you'd like me to try again, I'll open the pages one or two at a time so I stay under the limit, in this order:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word (Psalm 84), then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub or StudyLight, then Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** pages on Psalm 84 from Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and the Ligonier, Desiring God and 1517 sites. These will be most useful for verse 9 ("Your anointed") and verse 11 ("grace and glory," "no good thing").
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on "Valley of Baca" (v. 6) and "Gittith" (v. 1), and Augustine's sermon on New Advent. Older Catholic Bibles number this psalm 83, so I'll check for it under that number too. I'll also look for any site that discusses how prosperity teachers use verse 11.

Just say "continue" and I'll start with step 1.
